To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The cognitive radar architecture enables the fusion of modern radar technologies and cognitive mechanisms for enhanced radar performance in terms of target signature extraction”.

cognitive radar systems are capable of improving target parameter extraction in modern radar system designs like MIMO, ultra wideband and joint communication-radars by exploiting the dynamic radar environment through constant interactions.
the cognitive approach to radar design enables a better awareness and adaptation of modern radar system to their environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach for cognitive radar design.
the development of cognitive radar systems that are capable of learning from the environment and adapting to the changing radar scene.
the design of cognitive radar systems, which are able to dynamically adapt their operational parameters in accordance with the radar scene variations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cognitive radar architecture is a novel approach which enables the development of intelligent radar systems which are able to learn about their surroundings through interactions with the dynamic target scene.
this thesis has provided a theoretical framework for implementation of cognitive mechanisms in modern MIMO, U/WB, joint communication-radar, cognitive radio and cognitive radar network design.
the cognitive radar network design and implementation has the potential to significantly enhance the performance of modern radars in terms of target signature extraction and resource management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a cognitive architecture for modern radar systems which enables the adaptation of radar system parameters in accordance with the radar scene variations.
the proposed cognitive radar systems are capable to learn about the target scene variations and adapt their operational parameters in real-time.

the thesis provides a novel framework for implementing cognitive feedback in modern radars, which enables the adaptation of the operational parameters of the radar system to the dynamic target scene variations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cognitive mechanisms can be used to enhance the target detection, tracking, classification and parameter estimation performance of modern radar systems.
the cognitive feedback between the transmitter and receiver could be the facilitator of intelligent illumination strategies in modern radar system architectures.
the cognitive radar architecture provides an intelligent framework for the design of modern radars.
